answered.question: Should alpha be printed as a sixth component, or reported as drift with a warning when it exceeds the idiosyncratic term? (opened 2026-09-13)
answered.answer: Printed as a sixth component, WITH ITS STANDARD ERROR. Component.DRIFT shipped on main today (PR #70); Fit.intercept_se publishes the WLS standard error at the final Huber weights, and the estimation note appends 'N standard errors from zero' plus '(not distinguishable from zero)' below 1.96.
answered.proof: All nine names decompose exactly: market + drift + idiosyncratic sums to the realised local return to 1e-12. Every one of the nine drifts reads not distinguishable from zero, at 0.1 to 1.3 standard errors.
notes: The invariant test that should have caught this PASSED, because its own body added fit.coefficients[0] back in. The only written record of the defect was the workaround; logged as a new defect-log family, 'compensated-in-the-test' (details/07-DEFECT-LOG.md §19).
Only the intercept's error is published. The slopes are shrunk toward a prior AFTER fitting, so their fitted standard errors would not describe the coefficients actually reported.
This corrects my own 2026-09-13 page, which read the per-name alphas as economically legible. With errors attached they are noise.

lessons: A residual is only 'idiosyncratic' if every systematic factor has a column. With the sector beta fixed at 0, a sector-wide selloff is indistinguishable from company news, and the label asserts the difference the model cannot make.

The same defect can arrive twice in one system by different routes: alpha was computed and not printed, the sector factor is not computed at all. The first was fixable by reporting; the second needs data.

A coefficient without its standard error is a story waiting to be told. Yesterday's page read nine drifts as economically legible; tonight the same nine, with errors attached, are all noise - and nothing about the fits changed except what was printed.
A test can be the only written record of the defect it was meant to catch. The invariant held because the test compensated for the missing term in its own body; the workaround was the documentation.

A confirming observation written as a test is worth more than one written as a hope. The 09-13 page named the exact story it would take to raise confidence in Petronas Chemicals, and the next sweep produced it - which is why the confidence moved by a stated amount.

An alert that closes because the rule was wrong is a different event from one that closes because the data arrived, and a log that does not distinguish them teaches the wrong lesson about how healthy the system is.
A source can degrade from late to absent between two pages. nst_business was a cadence warning on Sunday and a 404 on Monday; only the page that reads both notices the direction.
